samples.summary: comment-ops.ts reimplements thread logic that `@wafflebase/sheets` already owns and exports
samples.evidence: `packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts` is the canonical pure thread module — `createThread`, `addReply`, `editComment`, `deleteComment` (root comment ⇒ delete thread, lines 61-76), `setThreadResolved` — and `createThread`/`addReply` are already re-exported from `packages/sheets/src/index.ts:373-374`, which the backend depends on and already imports from (`comments.controller.ts` imports `parseRef`, `cellAnchorToSref`, `Thread`, `CommentAuthor` from it). The new `comment-ops.ts` writes its own `buildThread`/`buildReply`/`applySetResolved`/`applyDeleteComment` instead of composing them, so the same rules now exist twice (a third near-identical copy already lives in `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts`). They have already diverged: sheets' `assertNonEmpty` deliberately preserves the body verbatim ('preserve newlines / leading-trailing spaces inside non-empty content'), while the API path trims via `normalizeBody`, so the editor and the API store different text for the same input, and any future change to the root-comment/resolve rules must be made in two (or three) places. The Yorkie BigInt boundary is a legitimate backend concern, but it could wrap the shared ops rather than replace them.

samples.summary: API-created comments/replies/resolves emit no notification, and notifications.md's stated premise ('comments never pass through the backend') is now false and unrecorded
samples.evidence: `docs/design/notifications.md:16-18` states comment events are 'reported by the client and authorized by the server' *because* 'comments live inside Yorkie CRDT documents and never pass through the backend, so the client is the only party that knows a comment was posted', with callers listed at lines 210-212 as the three frontend comment controllers posting `POST /notifications/comment`. This change makes the backend itself a comment writer, but `comments.controller.ts` never calls `NotificationService.createFromComment` on create/reply/resolve. Consequence outside the codebase: a thread an agent opens with an @mention, a reply to a human's comment, and a resolve of someone's thread all notify nobody, so a mentioned collaborator is never told — the exact event class notifications v1 exists to deliver. No design doc records the new writer or the decision to skip notification.

samples.summary: Slide ops replace the whole `root.slides` array, so the stated advantage over `PUT .../content` (surviving concurrent edits) is largely not delivered
samples.evidence: The controller's own rationale (lines 27-33 of the file, and the CLI comment at `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts` 'these four touch one slide each, so a concurrent edit elsewhere in the deck survives') claims these verbs avoid the lost-update problem of whole-document replace. But `apply()` reads the deck out of the CRDT, mutates a detached `MemSlidesStore` copy, and then assigns `root.slides = result.slides` — a wholesale replacement of the CRDT array object. Concurrent remote element/text edits inside other slides made in the same sync window are clobbered by that assignment, the same failure mode as `PUT content`, only narrowed from the whole root to the whole deck. A granular alternative exists in the shape the frontend Yorkie slides store uses (splice/insert on `root.slides` inside `doc.update`), and `MemSlidesStore` could still supply the constructed slide. Cost if real: silently lost collaborator work while an agent adds or moves a slide.

samples.evidence: `docs/design/rest-api.md` §5 enumerates the `/api/v1` surface route by route (tabs at lines 198-200: only GET/POST/PATCH; content at 303-307: 'word-processor documents only'; controller file tree at 564-568) and `docs/design/cli.md` §4 'Command Tree' (line 380ff) enumerates every command, including `sheets tabs list|create|rename` at 431-433 with no delete/move/duplicate, no `sheets images`, no `comments`, no `board`, no `slides slide|layouts`. samples.summary: Sheet comment creation is stricter than the editor and its stated rationale about the editor is inaccurate; the existing `ensureWorksheetExtent` helper was available
samples.evidence: `sheetCellAnchor` 400s when `rowOrder[r-1]`/`colOrder[c-1]` is absent, justified as 'the same reason the editor disables its comment button on an empty far-away cell'. The editor does no such thing: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:833` calls `storeRef.current?.ensureAxisOrder(activeCell.r, activeCell.c)` on selection (`yorkie-store.ts:657`), so any cell a user clicks acquires axis ids and can be commented on. `@wafflebase/sheets` already exports `ensureWorksheetExtent(ws, ref)` (`worksheet-grid.ts:72`) — the same helper the cell-write path reaches through `ensureWorksheetGrid` — so the API could materialize the axis exactly as the editor does. As shipped, 'comment on the empty cell next to the table' is rejected, and the code comment records a false premise about editor behavior.
searchedFor: grep ensureAxisOrder|createWorksheetAxisId in packages/frontend/src and packages/backend/src

samples.summary: The board content model is re-declared in the backend instead of reusing `@wafflebase/board`'s `BoardModel`
samples.evidence: `packages/board/src/model/board.ts:22-29` already defines the canonical board model (`meta: { title, unit?, recentColors? }`, `elements: Element[]`), and `packages/frontend/src/types/board-document.ts:3-10` mirrors it including the same `'Untitled board'` seed. `board-tree.ts` declares a third copy (`BoardMeta`/`BoardDocument`/`initialBoardRoot`) plus a hand-written `assertValidBoardBody` in `docs-content.controller.ts`. The backend has no `@wafflebase/board` dependency (`packages/backend/package.json` deps list docs/sheets/slides only), so this follows the existing `slides-tree.ts` precedent rather than breaking a rule — but the shape now exists in three places and any board meta field added to the package model will silently be dropped by the API's read/write path.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts is the canonical pure thread module with createThread (:11-28), addReply (:30-45), editComment (:47-59), deleteComment whose root-comment=>delete-thread rule sits at :65-76 (`if (idx === 0) return null;` :71), and setThreadResolved (:78-89); createThread/addReply are re-exported at packages/sheets/src/index.ts:373-374 (imported at :228). The backend genuinely depends on and imports from that package (comments.controller.ts:38-42; comment-ops.ts:2). Despite that, packages/backend/src/yorkie/comment-ops.ts re-encodes the same rules instead of composing them: buildThread (:113-132), buildReply (:134-145), applySetResolved (:155-169, same resolved/resolvedAt/resolvedBy + delete-on-unresolve semantics as setThreadResolved), and applyDeleteComment (:179-194) repeating the index-0 root-comment rule at :188-191. A third copy of the same rules exists at packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:112-126 and :128-145, and that frontend file is purely the Yorkie-write shim while yorkie-store.ts:23-24,1275,1300 composes the shared createThread/addReply from @wafflebase/sheets - i.e. the repo's own established pattern (shared pure ops + thin CRDT apply layer) is what the backend departs from. The claimed divergence is live, not hypothetical: normalizeBody trims (comment-ops.ts:203-207) and that trimmed text is what is stored (comments.controller.ts:166,193,214 and :235,239), while sheets' assertNonEmpty deliberately preserves the body verbatim (thread.ts:3-9, comment at :8), so the editor and the API persist different text for the same input, and the root-comment/resolve rules must now be maintained in three places. This is duplication that has already diverged and gives two answers to the same question - major under this lens. The one mitigating detail I found (sheets' createThread is typed to the concrete sheet-cell CommentAnchor, types.ts:7-12, so docs/PDF anchors cannot use it as-is) bears on how to reuse, not on whether the duplication is real, and does not apply to the spreadsheet path at all. No guard makes it unreachable and nothing is absent as described.

verdict.reason: The absence is real on both halves. (1) No notification is emitted for API-created comments: `comments.controller.ts` injects only DocumentService and YorkieService (:83-86) and contains no notification reference; a grep for NotificationService/createFromComment across packages/backend/src hits only workspace/, template/, and notification/ — never api/v1/ or yorkie/. The only comment-notification producers are frontend (`components/comments/notify.ts:125`), invoked after local editor writes in sheet-view.tsx:905/924/945, pdf-comments-controller.ts:43/62/86 and docs-comments-controller.ts, so a backend-written thread/reply/resolve has no reporter at all — an agent's @mention notifies nobody. (2) The premise is unrecorded: notifications.md:16-18 and 210-212 still assert comments "never pass through the backend" with the three frontend controllers as the only callers; agentic-office-workflow.md:213 still says "No comment controller under /api/v1"; backend/README.md:559-562 repeats it. rest-api.md has no comments/notification content, and the plan doc's docs step (20260904-class-b-backend-endpoints-todo.md:41-44) is unchecked with no notification decision in its Decisions section (:46-61). This sits in the design-fit lane (contradicted cross-subsystem premise plus a user-visible gap in the exact event class notifications v1 delivers), so I found no ground to refute.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out in full. `apply()` in slides.controller.ts:163-176 reads the deck out of the CRDT, mutates a detached `MemSlidesStore` copy (slide-ops.ts:72-79), and writes back with `root.slides = result.slides` — a wholesale replacement of the CRDT array container, not a granular mutation. The rationale the reviewer quotes is present verbatim at slides.controller.ts:36-49 and http-client.ts:574-576 ('these four touch one slide each, so a concurrent edit elsewhere in the deck survives'), and the container replacement does not deliver that: concurrent in-slide element/text edits land on the removed array subtree and are dropped, contradicting docs/design/rest-api.md:140-142 ('Yorkie's CRDT ensures that writes from the API merge conflict-free with live user edits'). The granular alternative the reviewer names genuinely exists in the shape the repo already uses: yorkie-slides-store.ts:734/793/803/818 splice `r.slides` inside `doc.update`. yorkie.service.ts:50-60 shows manual-sync attach then sync with no CAS or conflict guard, so nothing upstream makes this unreachable. The plan doc (20260904-class-b-backend-endpoints-todo.md:29-31, 58-60) justifies 'persist root.slides only' by preserving dropped `meta` fields and does not declare per-slide granularity a Non-Goal, so this is not sanctioned scope reduction. In-lane as approach fit / available-reuse, with a cost outside codebase tidiness (silently lost collaborator work), so it stays blocking.
